name: Vimal Shah
profile: Kenyan industrialist born 1960 who in 1985 turned his family's textile business into soap maker Bidco with his father B.D. Shah and brother Tarun. Bidco grew into East Africa's leading maker of edible oils, detergents, personal care and food brands, with JVs incl. Wilmar and Land O'Lakes. He handed the CEO role to Thiagarajan Ramamurthy and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: The Bidco name comes from his father's initials, B.D. (Shah); the company operates in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and Madagascar.
deep_cut_fact: His first job, taken while at university, was selling life insurance on commission; he recalled that only about three or four in 100 prospects bought. He calls himself a workaholic who works from 5am to midnight.
notes: happy@bidcoafrica.com is Bidco's general company contact, not a personal one. He speaks often at regional business events (e.g. Building Bridges); LinkedIn or company channels are the best route.

name: Peter Jackson
current_role: Filmmaker; founder of WingNut Films (Wellington, NZ); producer of 'The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum' (2027)
profile: New Zealand director behind the 'Lord of the Rings' and 'Hobbit' trilogies, which grossed about $6bn worldwide. He became a billionaire in 2021 after selling Weta Digital's tech to Unity for $1.6bn in cash and stock. He is now producing 'The Hunt for Gollum' (directed by Andy Serkis), writing a Tintin sequel with Fran Walsh, and has invested in de-extinction firm Colossal Biosciences.
interesting_fact: He owns more than 40 airworthy WWI-era aircraft, kept at Hood Aerodrome near Masterton, and his firm The Vintage Aviator restores and builds WWI/WWII fighters. He received an Honorary Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He left school at 16 to work for seven years as a photo-engraver at Wellington's Evening Post, living with his parents to save for film gear. He shot his debut 'Bad Taste' mostly at weekends with unpaid friends, and played two roles in it, including a cliff-top fight with himself.
notes: Weta Workshop's FAQ names reception@wingnutfilms.co.nz for all enquiries about Peter Jackson and WingNut Films. He is a big fan of aviation history and tech (Weta, de-extinction), which could be a good podcast angle. He rarely does interviews outside film promotion.

name: Chaijudh Karnasuta
current_role: Co-founder of Italian-Thai Development (ITD), Thailand; MarketScreener also lists him as chairman of Siam Steel Syndicate. Current status unverified.
profile: Forbes listed him in 1996 with about $1.9bn and no source of wealth. He is most likely the Thai co-founder (also spelled Chaiyudh) of Italian-Thai Development, which he started with Italian Giorgio Berlingieri in 1958. ITD became one of Thailand's largest construction groups and is now led by Premchai Karnasuta.
interesting_fact: Before founding ITD, he and Giorgio Berlingieri worked together in 1954 on a venture to salvage five sunken ships. ITD was incorporated on 15 August 1958.
notes: Only one Forbes listing (1996) with no source of wealth, so the ITD match is likely but not certain. He would be very elderly now and I could not confirm whether he is alive. ITD is currently led by Premchai Karnasuta, who faces criminal charges over a 2025 building collapse. Treat this lead with caution.

name: Kalen Jackson
current_role: Owner and chief brand officer, Indianapolis Colts; president, Indianapolis Colts Foundation
profile: Youngest daughter of the late Colts owner Jim Irsay; she and her two sisters each inherited about a third of the NFL franchise after his death in May 2025. She joined the team in 2010 after graduating from Indiana University in sports management and marketing. She now runs the Colts' brand and philanthropy, including the Kicking The Stigma mental health initiative.
interesting_fact: Kicking The Stigma, which she leads, has put more than $32m into mental health grants and programs since 2020. It won the Colts the 2025 ESPY for Sports Humanitarian Team of the Year.
deep_cut_fact: She worked with the Indiana High School Athletic Association to promote girls' flag football and get it made an official Indiana high school sport. She also helped set up the Irsay Institute at IU Bloomington, which researches mental health stigma. She chairs the NFL's employee benefits committee.
notes: She speaks publicly and often about mental health (GMFB, Up & Adam, BizVoice), so a podcast pitch tied to Kicking The Stigma is the most natural route, via Colts communications. There is no energy or data-center link. The official_website entry is the Colts front-office page, not her own site.

name: Zhang Huiming
current_role: Co-holder, with Wen Yibo, of the Sound Group environmental business (Sound Environment / Sound Global); no public executive role found
profile: Hurun listed her jointly with Wen Yibo (about $1.8bn, 2014-2020). Wen Yibo founded the Sound water and waste-treatment group in 1993 and chairs HK-listed Sound Global. HK filings show Zhang Huiming holding Sound Global shares through a spouse-interest designation, which suggests she is Wen's wife, but no source confirms this.
interesting_fact: In a March 2019 disclosure, GuruFocus shows Zhang Huiming with a 'spouse interest' in about 774 million Sound Global (HKSE: 00967) shares.
notes: Very low public profile; I found nothing on her as an individual. Wen Yibo is the operating founder, so any outreach would realistically go through the Sound group. Fell off the Hurun lists after 2020.

name: Alberto Cortina
current_role: Investor and major ACS shareholder; co-founder of the Fundación Alberto y Elena Cortina
profile: Madrid-born (1947) lawyer-turned-businessman. With his cousin Alberto Alcocer ('Los Albertos') he ran Construcciones y Contratas and built stakes in banking (Banco Zaragozano, sold to Barclays in 2003/04), ENCE and ACS. His fortune now rests mainly on his ACS stake, alongside other investments.
interesting_fact: He led the BDK financial group, which opened Banque de Dakar in Senegal in 2015. It is an unusual sub-Saharan banking venture for a Spanish construction-era tycoon.
deep_cut_fact: In 2012 he and his wife Elena Cué started a foundation that runs a social canteen, an 'Econosolidario' discount store and a 'comedor invisible' service delivering food to families' homes discreetly. It also sent food aid after the 2010 Haiti earthquake.
notes: He is 79 and keeps a low profile; the family foundation is the only published channel. Forbes facts mention the Panama Papers, so avoid that topic. ACS (Florentino Pérez) has big data-center and energy exposure, which could be a podcast angle.

name: Yan Jinggang
current_role: Former controller of Shanghai Zhongji (中技) Group; current role unknown
profile: Shanghai businessman whose Zhongji group began in building materials (concrete piles) and built a network of listed-company holdings, the 'Zhongji system'. That network included *ST Fukong (formerly Fortune Holdings). Hurun listed him at about $1.7bn in 2015-2018, before the group ran into heavy debt and lawsuits.
interesting_fact: In 2018 he agreed to sell 100% of Zhongji Group to Zhongshang Yunnan Asset Management, but that deal was terminated in January 2019.
notes: Not a suitable outreach target. Since 2018 he has been under a securities-regulator (CSRC) investigation and his group faced more than RMB 5bn in litigation (China Securities Journal, June 2018). I found no recent public activity and no contacts.

name: Mao Geping
current_role: Chairman, Mao Geping Cosmetics Co. (HKEX: 1318), Hangzhou
profile: Chinese makeup artist turned beauty mogul. He trained in Chinese opera, became famous doing TV makeup, and founded his eponymous premium cosmetics brand in 2000. He listed the company in Hong Kong in December 2024, raising more than $300m. The brand competes with international prestige labels in China, and his wife and sisters sit on the board.
interesting_fact: He became famous in 1994 as head makeup artist on the TV series 'Wu Zetian', where his technique turned actress Liu Xiaoqing into the empress across decades of her life. He has won four China Makeup Awards.
deep_cut_fact: Before building the brand, he founded the Mao Geping Image Design Art School in Hangzhou in 1998. In 2008 he opened a large campus in the Hangzhou Fashion Hub, the city's only creative hub dedicated to fashion and cosmetology. The school trains makeup artists, and they feed his counter network.
notes: The IR email is from the 2024 annual report's corporate information page. He mainly speaks to Chinese media. Weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast, but a good entrepreneurship story (opera student to HK-listed beauty brand).

name: famiy
current_role: (Likely Zhu Baoguo & family) Controlling shareholder of Joincare Pharmaceutical (~49% indirect), which controls Livzon Pharmaceutical. Zhu stepped down as chairman of both in Sept 2025.
profile: This record's name field is corrupted ('famiy'). It is a Hurun 2017 family entry tied to 'Joint Care' and shared with Zhu Baoguo, so most likely the Zhu Baoguo family of Joincare (健康元). Zhu founded Joincare in 1992 on the 'Madam Tai' women's-health oral liquid and later took control of Livzon. He resigned his chairmanships in September 2025 but still indirectly controls about 49% of Joincare.
interesting_fact: Joincare's origins lie in the 'Madam Tai' (太太口服液) oral liquid, a 1990s Chinese consumer health hit. Through Joincare, Zhu built control of Livzon, a major Hong Kong/Shenzhen-listed drugmaker.
notes: The record's name field is corrupted. It probably refers to Zhu Baoguo's family; see also any separate Zhu Baoguo record. Zhu is 60+ and now has no executive role. The Joincare website did not load, so no IR contact was captured.

name: Park Dong-suk
current_role: Founder and chairman/CEO, Sanil Electric (KOSPI-listed transformer maker)
profile: Korean engineer-entrepreneur who founded Sanil Electric after working at rival transformer maker Yuil Electric. He has spent 38 years on industrial special transformers and reactors. Sanil earns over 60-80% of revenue abroad, mainly from US utilities and grid players such as GE Vernova, PG&E and Duke Energy, and listed on KOSPI in 2024 on the grid and AI-power boom.
interesting_fact: Sanil Electric is a direct beneficiary of the US power-grid and data-center build-out. Most of its sales are exports of special transformers to US utilities and energy companies, and it won Korea's $100m Export Tower award.
deep_cut_fact: In August 2025 IBK Industrial Bank inducted him as the 22nd member of its Business Leaders' Hall of Fame. His guiding motto, as cited there, is 'Opportunity comes to those who are prepared' (기회는 준비된 사람에게 온다).
notes: Highly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast: transformers are a key grid bottleneck for AI data centers. Korean press says he started the business at 26 (founded Aug 1987); Forbes says 1994, so the founding year is unclear. The company website did not load, so no IR contact was captured; try Sanil Electric IR via KRX/DART filings.

name: Family Jahr
current_role: Hamburg publishing family; heirs of Gruner + Jahr co-founder John Jahr Sr.; held stake via Jahr Holding until 2014
profile: Very likely the Hamburg family of John Jahr Sr., who co-founded magazine publisher Gruner + Jahr (Stern, Brigitte, Geo) in 1965 with Richard Gruner and Gerd Bucerius. The family kept a 25.1% stake through Jahr Holding until Bertelsmann bought it out in November 2014. Family members have also held significant Henkel shares.
interesting_fact: At G+J's founding in 1965, John Jahr held 32.3%. After Gruner left in 1969, Jahr and Bucerius briefly owned the publisher 50/50 before Bertelsmann bought in.
notes: This is a family entry from a single 1996 Forbes listing; no individual is named. John Jahr Sr. died in 1991. The family sold its last G+J stake to Bertelsmann in 2014. Not an actionable outreach target without first picking a specific living family member.

name: Anas Sefrioui
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, Douja Promotion Groupe Addoha (Casablanca-listed); founder of Ciments de l'Atlas (CIMAT)
profile: Fès-born (1957) Moroccan developer who founded Addoha in 1988 and built it into Morocco's largest homebuilder through low-cost and social housing, often on government programmes. Addoha listed in Casablanca in 2006. He also built cement maker Ciments de l'Atlas, with plants in Morocco and West/Central Africa. The record's country (Macao) is wrong; he is Moroccan.
interesting_fact: Beyond housing, he built cement plants in Settat and Beni Mellal and 500,000-ton plants in Cameroon, Gabon, Ivory Coast and Guinea, expanding Addoha's model across francophone Africa.
deep_cut_fact: He left secondary school early to work in his father Haj Abdeslam Sefrioui's business making a clay product used to wash the body and hair (traditional Moroccan ghassoul). He used the savings from that to start his property group in 1988.
notes: The input country 'Macao' is wrong; he is Moroccan. He is media-shy, and his daughter Kenza is deputy chair. The listed contacts are Addoha's company channels and LinkedIn, not personal ones.

name: Wang Linpeng
profile: Former chairman of Beijing Easyhome (居然之家 / 居然智家), the home-furnishings retail chain he took over in 1999 and built into a national leader. Chinese Wikipedia reports he died on 27 July 2025, aged about 56.
notes: Deceased (July 27, 2025), per https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/汪林朋, which cites The Paper (澎湃新闻). Forbes now lists him as 'former'. Do not contact.

name: He Qi
current_role: Associated with 'Junhe' (trading), per Hurun; not independently verified
profile: Hurun Global listed He Qi (何旗) of China at about $1.4bn (2019-2025), with wealth from 'Junhe' in trading. I could not verify which Junhe company this is or confirm any biographical details.
notes: Unverified: the lane hit its web-search budget before this person, and Baidu Baike blocked automated access. Needs a follow-up search, e.g. Hurun profile '何旗 君和'. The name is common, so be careful matching.

name: Adrian Paval
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Dragoș), Dedeman and Pavăl Holding, Romania
profile: Adrian Pavăl and his brother Dragoș founded DIY and building-materials retailer Dedeman in Bacău in 1992. It grew into Romania's market leader, overtaking Praktiker in 2010, and now has about 60+ stores, over 12,000 staff and roughly $2bn in sales. Through Pavăl Holding they invest in offices in Bucharest and Cluj, listed Romanian stocks (Romgaz, Transelectrica, Banca Transilvania) and a private equity fund.
interesting_fact: Dedeman had just 11 employees in 1994 and over 12,000 today. About 85% of its 60,000+ in-store products come from Romanian suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: Their holding launched Grunman Energy to put solar power on the rooftops of Dedeman's seven logistics centres. They also hold stakes in grid operator Transelectrica and gas producer Romgaz, a quiet energy angle in a retail fortune.
notes: The Pavăl brothers are famously media-shy and rarely give interviews. The only published channel is Dedeman's corporate contact page. The energy holdings (Transelectrica, Romgaz, rooftop solar) offer a podcast hook.

name: Gao Xingjiang
current_role: Chairman, Yongxing Special Materials Technology (永兴材料, SZSE: 002756), Huzhou, Zhejiang
profile: A former PLA Navy serviceman (1981-87), he founded Yongxing in July 2000 as a maker of stainless steel and nickel-alloy bars and wire rods. It is a top-3 Chinese supplier, listed in 2015. He then pivoted the company into lithium: Yongxing mines lepidolite in Yichun, Jiangxi, is a leading Chinese producer of battery-grade lithium carbonate from mica, and also makes lithium-titanate batteries for storage.
interesting_fact: Yongxing has invested in 超磁新能 (Chaoci Xinneng, Shanghai), a high-temperature-superconducting magnet startup for fusion. It built its first HTS pancake coil and is working toward a 25-tesla toroidal-field model magnet for controlled fusion.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an industrialist, Gao served six years in the People's Liberation Army Navy (1981-1987).
notes: Strong energy angle: lithium carbonate, energy storage batteries and a fusion-magnet investment. The company site has an online message form; investor contact is also available via the SZSE interactive platform (互动易). Little English-language coverage of him personally.

name: Els Blokker
current_role: Shareholder/heir in the Blokker family retail holding (Blokker Holding / Mavaro); art patron
profile: Els Blokker-Verwer is the widow of Jaap Blokker (1942-2011), who ran Dutch retailer Blokker Holding from 1976 to 2010 and co-owned it with his brother Albert. She inherited a large stake and ranked 7th on the Quote 500 in 2013. The family later sold off most chains in the group.
interesting_fact: In April 2018 she donated the couple's Nardinc Collection of 117 Dutch modernist paintings to the Singer Laren museum. It includes about 40 works by Jan Sluijters plus Van Dongen, Gestel, Toorop and Willink, and the gift also funded a new museum wing.
deep_cut_fact: The collection's name, 'Nardinc', and a book about it, 'De gezamenlijke kunstliefde van Jaap en Els Blokker' ('Jaap and Els Blokker's shared love of art'), reflect that the couple built the collection together around Jan Sluijters.
notes: Very private, with no published contacts; Singer Laren is the only public link. I could not confirm whether she is alive. Not on recent rich lists after 2015. Weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Herbert Sy
current_role: Adviser to the board, SM Investments Corp.; director, SM Prime Holdings (Philippines)
profile: Second-youngest of the six children of the late SM founder Henry Sy Sr., who all hold posts in the conglomerate spanning retail, banking (BDO, China Bank), property, mining and hotels. Herbert is closely involved in the group's supermarket operations and sits on the SM Prime board. He holds a management degree from De La Salle University.
interesting_fact: In 2022 SM Investments agreed to buy Philippine Geothermal Production Co. in a $304m all-share deal to cut its carbon footprint, a notable energy move for a retail-and-property group.
notes: Low-profile Sy sibling who rarely gives interviews; the realistic route is SM Investments corporate communications/IR. The SM sites blocked automated access, so no contact was captured. The geothermal deal is the energy hook.

name: Vitali Machitski
current_role: Controlling shareholder of Vimetco NV, owner of 84% of Romanian aluminium smelter Alro Slatina; developer of Moscow's Rostec-City complex
profile: Russian businessman who traded timber and oil in the 1990s, sold refinery assets to Yukos and others in the early 2000s, and took control of Romania's privatised Alro aluminium smelter in 2002 via Marco Industries, later Vimetco. Vimetco also held stakes in China's Zhongfu Industrial. His companies developed the Rostec-City business complex in Moscow.
interesting_fact: Alro, his main asset, is Romania's single largest electricity consumer, using about 8% of national power. In 2007 it was the largest primary aluminium producer in Central and Eastern Europe outside the CIS.
notes: Very private, with no published personal contacts. Forbes notes he is a friend of Rostec head Sergey Chemezov, so check sanctions exposure before any outreach. Alive status was not confirmed independently but he is on the 2026 Forbes real-time list. Energy angle: aluminium smelting and power intensity.

name: Lidiya Mikhailova
current_role: Co-owner (about 15%) of Cherkizovo Group, Russia's largest meat producer; her sons Evgeny (chairman) and Sergei (CEO) run it
profile: Ex-wife of Cherkizovo founder Igor Babaev. He built the Moscow Cherkizovsky meat plant into Cherkizovo Group, which listed in London and Moscow in 2006, and later passed his shares to their sons. She holds about 15% alongside sons Evgeny and Sergei Mikhailov (about 28% each). The group has over 20,000 employees and about $3.4bn in 2025 revenue.
interesting_fact: Cherkizovo became a major poultry and pork producer through acquisitions; after buying LISKO Broiler in 2014 its poultry capacity reached about 550,000 tonnes a year. It trades on the Moscow Exchange as GCHE.
notes: Passive shareholder with no public profile; Forbes lists her as 'former' (2024). The company site blocked automated access, so no IR contact was captured. Russian-sanctions context applies, and this is not a useful podcast guest.
